method: Original PDF renders only. Every physical page viewed individually; opening/meter/final-pause details checked at 6×. No detector inventory, native plan, 109041 source map or output used as map authority. Counts follow actual vertical measure boundaries and printed subsequent starts.
durationScope: 176 numbered complete bars with a separate initial eighth-note upbeat; meter changes mean this is not 176 equal-duration bars. No repeats were observed. No generated rests or absent-part duration inference is needed.

systems.sourceObservations: One complete physical system. Full title, Goethe credit, six-part choir/orchestra subtitle, dedication, Brahms Op. 89 and publication 1883 text precede the music. Eighth-note upbeat before numbered bar 1; four complete C bars follow. All 20 part rows printed, including quiet combined Alto and Bass staves. Maestoso printed above Flutes and below Double Bass. Local pesante does not authorize broadcasting to quiet choir.

One physical system; all 20 part rows printed. Alto I–II and Bass I–II remain on one quiet staff each. Printed start 5. Active orchestral slurs, ledger notes, accents and dynamics require their original source extents.

Alto I/II and Bass I/II split into separate staves: 22 physical staves, 20 part rows. Both pairs remain split on every later page. Rehearsal A at bar 18. Tenor and Bass enter late in bar 19. Shared Bass lyric under the upper member must accompany the complete paired Bass row.
Printed start 21; Soprano and both Altos enter late in bar 21. Alto/Bass lyric underlay is partly shared between the pair. Five complete C bars.
Printed start 26. Both Alto and Bass pairs are present, even where one or both members rest; do not infer omission from silence.
Printed start 31. Rehearsal B at bar 35. All six vocal staves and all orchestral staves present; high ledger notes and slurs extend outside staff cores.
Printed start 37. Six vocal staves; Alto and Bass pairs retain shared or separate printed lyric underlay as engraved.
Printed start 42. Both Bass voices have separate lyric lines in parts of this system; preserve both. Viola changes clef within the system and at its right end.
Printed start 47. Rehearsal C at bar 48. Violin II has printed 6. and 12. division indications at the new section; retain in that part rather than treating as measure labels.
Printed start 53. Long vocal ties, lyric extension dashes and lower dynamics near interstaff boundaries are owned notation, not removable line residue.
Printed start 58. Rehearsal D at bar 60. Lyric phrases increasingly independent across Alto/Bass pairs. Local p dol. and dim. remain with their actual instrument.

Printed start 64. Distinct lyrics on both Alto and Bass staves. Low Violin II slurs and Viola upper notation approach the intervening space; a narrow horizontal gap alone cannot certify crop separation.
Printed start 70. Paired Alto/Bass staves continue; some common lyric lines coexist with separate printed lines.
Printed start 76. Rehearsal E at bar 80. Sempre più f is printed on the six choir staves approaching the bar-80 entrance; keep at its actual within-system position.

Printed start 82. Key-signature change at bar 84. Molto marcato belongs to the active low instrumental lines (Bassoons, Contrabassoon, Trombone III/Tuba, Cello and Double Bass), not the adjacent silent Timpani row.
Printed start 87. Rehearsal F at bar 90. Local dolce on Violin I/II at the late passage; printed player numerals distinguish instrument members.
Printed start 93. Seven full C bars, with cancellation/new key signs at the terminal boundary preparing bar 100. Ties and lyric extensions continue through the page edge.

Printed start 100. P sotto voce appears at each choir entry. Pizz. at the left belongs only to Double Bass: the Cello passage remains under bowed slurs. Retain the spelling/position and avoid foreign instruction carryover.
Printed start 106. Pizz. appears in each string part at the final beat of bar 110. Local poco cresc./cresc. are individually printed; preserve the quiet upper-string source rows before their entry.

Printed start 111. Five C bars (111–115), followed by three 3/4 bars (116–118), with quarter-note = quarter-note equivalence above Flutes and below Double Bass. Sehr weich und gebunden is printed above the choir at bar 116; do not misattribute it to silent Timpani. Arco at late bar 111 belongs to the individual strings. Horns I–II long upper slur crest must remain intact.
Printed start 119. Eleven full 3/4 bars. P dolcissimo appears on entering winds/Horns I–II and upper strings/Cello, not all silent instrument rows. Tenor espress. entry at the final bar is local.
Printed start 130. Eleven full 3/4 bars. Rehearsal G at system start. Soprano and all strings are printed silent rows; other vocal voices continue independent lyrics.

Printed start 141. Twelve full 3/4 bars. Rehearsal H at bar 144. String pizz. at bar 144; the later arco belongs to Cello alone (late bar 147), not Viola above. Preserve the first-bar Trombones I–II dim. including the period and full descender. Choir p espress. and all lyric underlay retain their actual ownership.

Printed start 153. Nine 3/4 bars through 161, then common time at bar 162. First flute changes to piccolo at the late bar-161 entry; keep the player/instrument label. Con sordini appears for Violin I, Violin II, Viola and Cello at bar 160, not Double Bass. Upper strings pp sempre, ma marcato; retain source instruction scope. Separate Alto/Bass staves continue.

Printed start 163. Five common-time bars. 2. gr. Flöte marks the second large flute entry late in bar 165; it is not a generic tempo heading. Alto/Bass pair members have different lyrics and entries; preserve both.

Printed start 168. Nine common-time bars to final bar 176. First piccolo reentry, second large-flute line, Double Bass arco at bar 170, local perdendosi and all final fermatas/pp dynamics must remain. Cello and Double Bass low slurs and nearby dynamics overlap vertical context; simple staff-midpoint cuts would be unsafe. Final numbered bar is a full common-time sustained/rest bar, not a complementary shortened pickup bar.
